## Summary

Found and fixed the reason **nothing downstream could consume the widened R2 carrier** — a defect four prior sessions on this task had missed, three of them mine. The widening was already landed; the gap was measured, not guessed: outside the twenty `DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` files, `DivFamZarAff` appeared **nowhere in the tree**.

The cause is that one operation has two faces. `DivFamZarAff` had `mapAlg` (instance-tower) but not `mapAlgHom` (explicit-map), and the vehicle `divFamZar` indexes its compatibility by `Over.resAlgHom` — a bare `AlgHom` with no tower instance. The faces are interderivable in a few lines, which is exactly why audits comparing the widened layer to the chart-typed one *by name* read as complete.

## Progress
- `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFace.lean`: new, 191L, 0 sorries — `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom`, functor laws, the face-change bridge both ways, `picClass_mapAlgHom`, `congr`, `toAff_mapAlgHom`.
- `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffVehicle.lean`: new, 292L, 0 sorries — `divFamZarAff`, its section API, `divFamZarAffAffineEquiv`, and the comparison from the chart-typed vehicle.
- `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffGlueZarKit.lean`: new, 661L, 0 sorries — the assembly restated at **bare** local-equation systems, after measuring that the chart-typed version's *statement* demands a full certificate while its *body* projects only `.eqns` and `.cover`.
- `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffGlueZar.lean`: new, 302L, 0 sorries — `DivFamZarAff.exists_glue_of_away_compat`. **The widened value is a Zariski sheaf value**, with no `|P¹(k)|` hypothesis anywhere.
- `Picard/DivisorFamilyZariskiGlue.lean`: docstring only — pointer to the general form it is now definitionally subsumed by.
- `informal/spec-dd-r.md`: ADDENDUM 8 §§8.1–8.7; ADDENDUM 6 item 1 and ADDENDUM 7 §7.5 marked in place.

Ten CAS commits, all ancestors of HEAD. Axiom-clean against a `sorryAx` control that fires; `lake build` 8838 jobs exit 0.

## Issues
**Three self-corrections.** "Residue = one statement" was true of the certificate, not the lane. A commit message described a 110-line file that grew to 646 between my read and the commit. Two docstrings advertised declarations that didn't exist.

**A fresh-context review found three more, all fixed:** "thirteen files" was twenty; "the consumer stack is spelled entirely at `mapAlgHom`" was overstated (`divFunctor` and `DivRepGlobalData` mention it zero times); and an inherited vacuity justification was **false** — both spellings are equivalent at every carrier used. It also confirmed a composition I'd asserted without landing, and flagged ~300 lines now duplicated.

**Worth carrying:** the keystone file was **red with zero sorries** — `eq_of_away_eq` takes `n` explicitly where the chart-typed one has it implicit, surfacing as an unresolvable `l.down` naming neither.

Filed I-0617, I-0618, I-0631; completed I-0643. Answered ajc-rr's cone question with a measurement (59 modules, 16071 lines) and flagged a harmless phantom deletion in ajcr-w5-av's path without touching it.

## Why I stopped
**Substantially advanced; deliberately not marked done.** Residue is two items: (a) the subordinate Stacks 0B8B input, out of scope per I-0492 clause 2 — and I verified it's a genuine gap, not a restatement of its own conclusion; (b) `divFamZarAff.map` plus `divFunctorAff`, now priced at ~350 transcribed lines with two of three bricks already elaborated.

Full builds were repeatedly unavailable under eight-lane contention; per-file `lake env lean` and targeted `lake build` covered every file I touched. Both advisory inbox ceilings remain exceeded, deliberately and recorded as such.

# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)

Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
workspace.

## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)

All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:

```bash
cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>

Archon-Commit: agent
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
```

If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.

### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)

**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
reverting everything that landed in the window.

**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
from §1b's shared-index staleness.

**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.

**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**

```bash
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
```

Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.

### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed

Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).

The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
the shared index drifts behind.

Consequences, all three binding:

1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).

Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.

## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
```

Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".

98	arbitrary morphism of test objects has a value at every affine open of the source,
99	glued over a finite basic-open refinement subordinate to the preimages of affine
100	opens — the S5b gluing keystone through `divFamZar.exists_glue_of_basic_compat`. -/
101	theorem exists_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
102	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃ v, IsPullbackValue C π n f s W v := by
103	  classical
104	  -- the basic refinement subordinate to preimages of affine opens
105	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W.2
106	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens, U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
107	    (fun w _ => by
108	      obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hfwV, -⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
109	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens (show f.left.base w ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
110	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V, hfwV, ⟨⟨V, hVaff⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
111	  have hsub' : ∀ r ∈ sub, ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens,
112	      T'.left.basicOpen r ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := fun r hr => by
113	    obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V, rfl⟩, hle⟩ := hsub r hr
114	    exact ⟨V, hle⟩
115	  choose Vc hVc using hsub'
116	  have hbmul : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
117	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
118	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
119	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
120	    exact inf_le_left
121	  have hbmul' : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
122	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
123	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
124	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
125	    exact inf_le_right
126	  -- glue the local pullbacks over the basic refinement
127	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := exists_glue_of_basic_compat W sub hspan
128	    (fun r : ↥sub => DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
129	      (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r.1 r.2).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r.1) (hVc r.1 r.2))
130	      (s.1 (Vc r.1 r.2)))
131	    hbmul hbmul'
132	    (fun r r' => by
133	      -- the overlap compatibility, from choice independence
134	      rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp,
135	        Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
136	      exact mapAlgHom_appLE_eq C π n f s (W₀ := ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen (r.1 * r'.1)⟩) _ _)
137	  -- the glued value has the pullback property
138	  refine ⟨z, fun W₀ hW₀ V hV => ?_⟩
139	  obtain ⟨sub₀, hspan₀, hsub₀⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
140	    (fun U₀ => ∃ r ∈ sub, U₀ = T'.left.basicOpen r)
141	    (fun w hw => by
142	      have hwW : w ∈ (⨆ r ∈ (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)), T'.left.basicOpen r) := by
143	        rw [iSup_basicOpen_of_span_eq_top _ _ hspan]
144	        exact hW₀ hw
145	      obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hwW
146	      obtain ⟨hrsub, hwr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hr
147	      exact ⟨T'.left.basicOpen r, hwr, ⟨r, hrsub, rfl⟩⟩)
148	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W₀ sub₀ hspan₀ (fun q hq => ?_)
149	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨r, hr, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub₀ q hq
150	  -- the left side restricts through the glued datum
151	  have hzr : DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
152	        (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) z
153	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
154	          (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r) (hVc r hr))
155	          (s.1 (Vc r hr)) := hz ⟨r, hr⟩
156	  have hL : DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le q))
157	      (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀) z)
158	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen q)
159	          (hqle.trans (hVc r hr))) (s.1 (Vc r hr)) := by
160	    rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp,
161	      show ((T'.left.basicOpen_le q).trans hW₀ :
162	          T'.left.basicOpen q ≤ W.1)
163	        = (hqle.trans (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) from rfl,
164	      ← Over.resAlgHom_comp T' hqle (T'.left.basicOpen_le r),
165	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, hzr, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp,
166	      Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
167	  -- the right side restricts directly
168	  rw [hL, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
169	  exact mapAlgHom_appLE_eq C π n f s (W₀ := ⟨_, W₀.2.basicOpen q⟩) _ _
170	
171	/-- Existence and uniqueness of the glued value. -/
172	theorem existsUnique_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
173	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃! v, IsPullbackValue C π n f s W v := by
174	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_isPullbackValue f s W
175	  exact ⟨v, hv, fun v' hv' => pullbackValue_unique hv' hv⟩

181	/-- The value of the restricted family at an affine open of the source. -/
182	noncomputable def mapVal (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
183	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, W.1) π n :=
184	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose

186	lemma mapVal_spec (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
187	    IsPullbackValue C π n f s W (mapVal C π n f s W) :=
188	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose_spec.1
189	
190	lemma mapVal_eq_of (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
191	    {v : DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, W.1) π n} (hv : IsPullbackValue C π n f s W v) :
192	    mapVal C π n f s W = v :=
193	  pullbackValue_unique (mapVal_spec C π n f s W) hv
194	
195	/-- The value of the restricted family on an affine open lying in the preimage of an
196	affine open is the plain pullback — no gluing. -/
197	lemma mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
198	    {W : T'.left.affineOpens} {V : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :
199	    mapVal C π n f s W
200	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 hV) (s.1 V) := by
201	  have h := mapVal_spec C π n f s W W le_rfl V hV
202	  rwa [Over.resAlgHom_rfl, DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id] at h
203	
204	/-- **Restriction of the locally certified vehicle along an arbitrary morphism of test
205	objects** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6 on the Addendum-2 carrier; the `picEtMap`
206	pattern): the value at each affine open of the source is the glued pullback value. -/
207	noncomputable def map (f : T' ⟶ T) : divFamZar C π n T → divFamZar C π n T' :=
208	  fun s =>
209	    ⟨fun W => mapVal C π n f s W, by
210	      intro U V h
211	      beta_reduce
212	      refine (mapVal_eq_of C π n f s (W := U) ?_).symm
213	      intro W₀ hW₀ V' hV'
214	      rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp]
215	      exact mapVal_spec C π n f s V W₀ (hW₀.trans h) V' hV'⟩
216	
217	@[simp]
218	lemma map_val (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
219	    (map C π n f s).1 W = mapVal C π n f s W :=
220	  rfl
221	
222	/-- The functor law: restriction along the identity is the identity. -/
223	theorem map_id (s : divFamZar C π n T) : map C π n (𝟙 T) s = s := by
224	  refine ext fun W => ?_
225	  rw [map_val]
226	  refine mapVal_eq_of C π n (𝟙 T) s ?_
227	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
228	  have hV' : W₀.1 ≤ V.1 := by
229	    intro p hp
230	    have hmem := hV hp
231	    rw [Over.id_left] at hmem
232	    exact hmem
233	  rw [Over.appLEAlgHom_id T V.1 W₀.1 hV hV', s.compat W₀ W hW₀, s.compat W₀ V hV']
234	
235	/-- The functor law: restriction along a composite is the composite of the
236	restrictions. -/
237	theorem map_comp (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T'' ⟶ T') (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
238	    map C π n (g ≫ f) s = map C π n g (map C π n f s) := by
239	  classical
240	  refine ext fun W => ?_
241	  rw [map_val, map_val]
242	  refine (mapVal_eq_of C π n (g ≫ f) s ?_)
243	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
244	  -- refine by basic opens whose `g`-image lies in an affine open inside `f⁻¹ V`
245	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
246	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V'' : T'.left.affineOpens,
247	      V''.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ U₀ = g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V''.1)
248	    (fun w hw => by
249	      have hgw : g.left.base w ∈ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := by
250	        have := hV hw
251	        rw [Over.comp_left] at this
252	        exact this
253	      obtain ⟨V'', hV''aff, hgwV'', hV''le⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
254	        T'.left.isBasis_affineOpens hgw
255	      exact ⟨g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'', hgwV'', ⟨⟨V'', hV''aff⟩, hV''le, rfl⟩⟩)
256	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W₀ sub hspan (fun q hq => ?_)
257	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V'', hV''le, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub q hq
258	  -- the left side, through the two glued values
259	  have hL : DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T'' (T''.left.basicOpen_le q))
260	      (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T'' hW₀)
261	        (mapVal C π n g (map C π n f s) W))
262	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom g V''.1 (T''.left.basicOpen q) hqle)
263	          (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 V''.1 hV''le) (s.1 V)) := by
264	    rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp,
265	      mapVal_spec C π n g (map C π n f s) W ⟨_, W₀.2.basicOpen q⟩
266	        ((T''.left.basicOpen_le q).trans hW₀) V'' hqle,
267	      map_val, mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom C π n f s hV''le]
268	  rw [hL, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp,
269	    Over.appLEAlgHom_comp f g V.1 V''.1 (T''.left.basicOpen q) hV''le hqle
270	      (hqle.trans ((g.left.preimage_mono hV''le).trans
271	        (le_of_eq (by rw [Over.comp_left, Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage])))),
272	    Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
273

282	/-- The affine comparison intertwines the section-ring pullback along `Spec` of an
283	algebra map with the algebra map itself (local copy of the `PicEtMap` helper). -/
284	private lemma overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) :
285	    (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
286	      (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ) (overSpecTopAffine A).1
287	        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
288	      = φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom := by
289	  have key : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
290	        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).hom
291	      = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).hom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom := by
292	    have h₁ : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
293	          (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top
294	        = (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)).appTop :=
295	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
296	    rw [h₁]
297	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)
298	  ext x
299	  exact congr($(key).hom x)
300	
301	/-- **Naturality of the affine comparison**: over affine tests, `divFamZar.map` along
302	`Spec` of an algebra map corresponds to the affine-level `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom` under
303	the comparison equivalences — the `picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` mirror, the agreement
304	of the glued general-test restriction with the S5b total base change. -/
305	theorem divFamZarAffineEquiv_naturality (φ : A →ₐ[k] B)
306	    (s : divFamZar C π n (overSpec k A)) :
307	    divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n B (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.overSpecMap φ) s)
308	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ (divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n A s) := by
309	  rw [divFamZarAffineEquiv_apply, divFamZarAffineEquiv_apply, divFamZar.map_val]
310	  have hval := divFamZar.mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom C π n (Over.overSpecMap φ) s
311	    (W := overSpecTopAffine B) (V := overSpecTopAffine A) le_top
312	  rw [hval]
313	  calc DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom
314	        (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
315	          (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
316	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)))
317	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
318	          (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
319	            (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top))
320	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _).symm
321	    _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)
322	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
323	        rw [overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp φ]
324	    _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
325	          (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A))) :=
326	        DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _
327	
328	end AffineNaturality

11	# The basic-open toolkit for the locally certified vehicle's functoriality (DD-2 S6a)
12	
13	The general-test functoriality and sheaf statements of the locally certified vehicle
14	`divFamZar` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMap` / `…ZarSheaf`) evaluate
15	compatible families on finite basic-open refinements of affine opens — the `picEtMap`

17	section rings of a basic cover of an affine open, translated onto the explicit
18	`Over.resAlgHom` face through the face-change bridge `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg`:
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZar.eq_of_basic_eq`: **separation over a basic cover** —
21	  two locally certified classes over `Γ(U)` agreeing on every member of a spanning
22	  family of basic opens agree (`DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq` at

26	  cover** — classes on the members of a spanning family of basic opens compatible on
27	  the multiplicative overlaps glue to a class on `Γ(U)`
28	  (`DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`, with the overlap carriers
29	  `Γ(basicOpen (r·r'))` receiving the member section rings by restriction).

31	  restriction of a vehicle section through two different affine opens of the target

60	/-- **Separation over a basic cover**: two locally certified divisor classes over the
61	sections of an affine open agreeing on every member of a finite spanning family of
62	basic opens agree — the S5b separation keystone `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq` instantiated
63	at the basic-open section-ring localizations, read on the explicit `Over.resAlgHom`
64	face through the face-change bridge. -/
65	theorem eq_of_basic_eq {T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (W : T'.left.affineOpens)
66	    (sub : Finset Γ(T'.left, W.1))
67	    (hs : Ideal.span (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)) = ⊤)
68	    {x y : DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, W.1) π n}
69	    (h : ∀ r ∈ sub,
70	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) x
71	        = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) y) :
72	    x = y := by
73	  classical
74	  haveI hAway : ∀ r : ↥sub, IsLocalization.Away (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))
75	      Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))) := fun r =>
76	    W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))
77	  haveI htow : ∀ r : ↥sub, IsScalarTower k Γ(T'.left, W.1)
78	      Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))) := fun r =>
79	    Over.isScalarTower_sections_basicOpen T' W.1 (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))
80	  refine DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq (fun r : ↥sub => (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
81	    (fun r : ↥sub => Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))) ?_
82	    (fun r => ?_)
83	  · rw [show (Set.range fun r : ↥sub => (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))) = (↑sub : Set _) from
84	      Subtype.range_coe]
85	    exact hs
86	  · rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
87	        (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))))
88	        (fun _ => rfl) x,
89	      ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
90	        (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))))
91	        (fun _ => rfl) y]
92	    exact h r r.2

94	/-! ## Gluing over the section rings of a basic cover -/
95	
96	/-- **Gluing over a basic cover**: locally certified divisor classes on the members of
97	a finite spanning family of basic opens of an affine open, compatible on the
98	multiplicative overlaps, glue to a class over the ambient sections restricting to
99	each — the S5b gluing keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat` instantiated at
100	the basic-open section-ring localizations, with the overlap carriers
101	`Γ(basicOpen (r·r'))` receiving the member section rings by restriction, read on the
102	explicit `Over.resAlgHom` face through the face-change bridge.  (Uniqueness is
103	`divFamZar.eq_of_basic_eq`.) -/
104	theorem exists_glue_of_basic_compat {T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (W : T'.left.affineOpens)
105	    (sub : Finset Γ(T'.left, W.1))
106	    (hspan : Ideal.span (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)) = ⊤)
107	    (v : ∀ r : ↥sub, DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))) π n)
108	    (hmul : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
109	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))

204	opens of the target gives the same locally certified class on any affine open of the
205	source contained in both preimages — the well-definedness of the glued functoriality
206	(`picEt.mapAlg_appLE_eq`, verbatim on the `DivFamZar` values). -/
207	theorem mapAlgHom_appLE_eq {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
208	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) {W₀ : T'.left.affineOpens}
209	    {V V' : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
210	    (hV' : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'.1) :
211	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV) (s.1 V)
212	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V'.1 W₀.1 hV') (s.1 V') := by
213	  classical
214	  -- refine by basic opens whose image lies in an affine open inside `V ⊓ V'`
215	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
216	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V'' : T.left.affineOpens,
217	      V''.1 ≤ V.1 ∧ V''.1 ≤ V'.1 ∧ U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V''.1)
218	    (fun w hw => by
219	      have hfw : f.left.base w ∈ V.1 ⊓ V'.1 := ⟨hV hw, hV' hw⟩
220	      obtain ⟨V'', hV''aff, hwV'', hV''le⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
221	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens hfw
222	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'', hwV'', ⟨⟨V'', hV''aff⟩,
223	        hV''le.trans inf_le_left, hV''le.trans inf_le_right, rfl⟩⟩)
224	  choose V'' hV''₁ hV''₂ hU₀ using fun (r : Γ(T'.left, W₀.1)) (hr : r ∈ sub) =>
225	    (hsub r hr).choose_spec.1
226	  have hDle : ∀ (r : Γ(T'.left, W₀.1)) (hr : r ∈ sub),
227	      T'.left.basicOpen r ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ (V'' r hr).1 := fun r hr => by
228	    have h1 := (hsub r hr).choose_spec.2
229	    rw [hU₀ r hr] at h1
230	    exact h1
231	  refine eq_of_basic_eq W₀ sub hspan (fun r hr => ?_)
232	  -- both sides restrict to the value at `V'' r hr` on the basic piece
233	  have hcalc : ∀ (Vb : T.left.affineOpens) (hVb : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ Vb.1)
234	      (hb₁ : (V'' r hr).1 ≤ Vb.1),
235	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r))
236	        (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f Vb.1 W₀.1 hVb) (s.1 Vb))
237	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
238	          (Over.appLEAlgHom f (V'' r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r) (hDle r hr))
239	          (s.1 (V'' r hr)) := by
240	    intro Vb hVb hb₁
241	    rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom,
242	      ← Over.appLEAlgHom_comp_resAlgHom f (T'.left.basicOpen r) hb₁
243	        (hDle r hr) ((T'.left.basicOpen_le r).trans hVb),
244	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, s.compat (V'' r hr) Vb hb₁]
245	  rw [hcalc V hV (hV''₁ r hr), hcalc V' hV' (hV''₂ r hr)]
246

8	/-!
9	# The widened vehicle and divisor functor: carrying a widened class to a GENERAL test
10	
11	`divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation` (`…AffAssemble.lean`) is the endpoint of
12	the widened certificate lane, and what it returns is a class **at an affine test**
13	`DivFamZarAff C R n`.  Every DD-R consumer is stated against a *functor* on the whole slice
14	over `Spec k`, so between the lane's endpoint and its consumers sits the affine-opens limit —
15	the `divFamZar` vehicle of `DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean` — and that layer had no widened
16	counterpart.  This file supplies it, following the chart-typed template line for line.
17	
18	## The shape, and why it is unchanged by R2
19	
20	A section over a test `T` is a family of widened classes, one per affine open of `T.left`,
21	compatible under restriction.  R2 widened where the pieces live **on the curve**; it changed
22	nothing about the Zariski structure of the **base**.  So the vehicle's shape is literally the
23	old one with `DivFamZar` replaced by `DivFamZarAff` and `mapAlgHom` by the widened face of
24	`…AffFace.lean` — which is precisely why that face had to exist first.
25	
26	`[IsProper C.hom]` is carried throughout: the widened base change needs it (an arbitrary affine
27	open's overlaps are not affine by fiat), and it is a hypothesis the DD-R lane has everywhere.
28	
29	## What this file does NOT do, stated precisely
30	
31	It defines the widened vehicle and proves its affine collapse.  It does **not** define the
32	restriction `divFamZarAff.map` along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, and therefore does
33	not define the widened *functor* either.  That is the remaining item of the R2 lane
34	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 8 §8.3 item 2): its input is the widened form of the base-side
35	Zariski gluing keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`
36	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarGlue.lean`), which should port because R2 left the base side alone —
37	but "should port" is a price, not a result, and nothing here assumes it.
38	
39	So a consumer can today be given a widened section over an **affine** test, and the general-test
40	statement is still owed.  Saying which is which is the point of this paragraph: a docstring that
41	advertises declarations a file does not contain is its own failure mode, and this tree has
42	already been bitten by it once.
43	
44	The comparison from the chart-typed side, `divFamZarToAffVehicle` below, does exist, and it goes
45	old → new only — the direction R2 asserts.  The converse is exactly what R2 says fails.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48	
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff` — the widened affine-opens limit at an arbitrary test.
50	* `divFamZarAff.eval`, `divFamZarAff.compat`, `divFamZarAff.ext` — the section API.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffAffineEquiv` — on an affine test the limit collapses to
52	  `DivFamZarAff` of the test algebra.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarToAffVehicle` — the comparison of vehicles, with
54	  `divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_toAffVehicle` for its coherence with the two affine collapses.
55	-/

    [∀ i j, Algebra (S i) (T i j)] [∀ i j, Algebra (S j) (T i j)]

/-- **Zariski separation of the widened divisor functor**: two widened classes agreeing under

    [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (S i)]
    [∀ i, IsScalarTower k R (S i)] [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]

  refine DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ?_

    (fun i => d₁.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i) n)
    (fun i => d₂.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i) n)
    (fun i => ?_)

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.

        (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))))

`divFamZarAff.eq_of_basic_eq`.) -/

    (hspan : Ideal.span (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)) = ⊤)

        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
    (hcompat : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (hmul r r')) (v r)
        = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (hmul' r r')) (v r')) :

/-! ## Choice independence of the glued evaluation -/

variable (C n) in
/-- **Choice independence**: restricting a widened vehicle section through two different affine
opens of the target gives the same widened locally certified class on any affine open of the
source contained in both preimages — the well-definedness of the glued functoriality
(`divFamZar.mapAlgHom_appLE_eq`, verbatim on the `DivFamZarAff` values). -/
theorem mapAlgHom_appLE_eq {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (s : divFamZarAff C n T) {W₀ : T'.left.affineOpens}
    {V V' : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
    (hV' : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'.1) :
    DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV) (s.1 V)
      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V'.1 W₀.1 hV') (s.1 V') := by
  classical
  -- refine by basic opens whose image lies in an affine open inside `V ⊓ V'`
  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
    (fun U₀ => ∃ V'' : T.left.affineOpens,
      V''.1 ≤ V.1 ∧ V''.1 ≤ V'.1 ∧ U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V''.1)
    (fun w hw => by
      have hfw : f.left.base w ∈ V.1 ⊓ V'.1 := ⟨hV hw, hV' hw⟩
      obtain ⟨V'', hV''aff, hwV'', hV''le⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens hfw
      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'', hwV'', ⟨⟨V'', hV''aff⟩,
        hV''le.trans inf_le_left, hV''le.trans inf_le_right, rfl⟩⟩)
  choose V'' hV''₁ hV''₂ hU₀ using fun (r : Γ(T'.left, W₀.1)) (hr : r ∈ sub) =>
    (hsub r hr).choose_spec.1
  have hDle : ∀ (r : Γ(T'.left, W₀.1)) (hr : r ∈ sub),
      T'.left.basicOpen r ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ (V'' r hr).1 := fun r hr => by
    have h1 := (hsub r hr).choose_spec.2
    rw [hU₀ r hr] at h1
    exact h1

  have hcalc : ∀ (Vb : T.left.affineOpens) (hVb : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ Vb.1)
      (hb₁ : (V'' r hr).1 ≤ Vb.1),
      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r))
        (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f Vb.1 W₀.1 hVb) (s.1 Vb))
      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom

          (s.1 (V'' r hr)) := by
    intro Vb hVb hb₁

      ← Over.appLEAlgHom_comp_resAlgHom f (T'.left.basicOpen r) hb₁
        (hDle r hr) ((T'.left.basicOpen_le r).trans hVb),
      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, s.compat (V'' r hr) Vb hb₁]
